reasoning: The general problem — that LLM-judge verdicts depend on judge model choice, yielding low inter-evaluator agreement and headline-number swings — is well established and routinely quantified with Krippendorff's alpha across multiple judge backbones on fixed generator outputs (e.g., the "Moral Mazes" pairwise-judge alpha analysis, "Rating Roulette," "Can You Trust LLM Judgments?", and the AF "Robustness of Model-Graded Evaluations" work). The scheming-specific instantiation is also partly covered: "Constitutional Black-Box Monitoring for Scheming in LLM Agents" evaluates several judge models for scheming detection and reports cross-judge variance (mean pAUROC variance < 0.02), and Apollo/OpenAI report grader-judge accuracy checks. However, that work measures detection accuracy against ground truth with frontier judges; I found no published study that specifically computes inter-judge agreement (Krippendorff's alpha) plus per-judge leniency offsets across several OPEN judges on a FROZEN scheming-transcript set and demonstrates the resulting swing in the headline scheming rate. The specific packaging is an unexplored but incremental gap.

evidence.title: Rating Roulette: Self-Inconsistency in LLM-As-A-Judge Frameworks
evidence.summary: Documents instability and self-inconsistency of LLM judges, establishing that verdicts depend heavily on the judge rather than the item — the core problem the proposal targets, in the general case.

evidence.title: Can You Trust LLM Judgments? Reliability of LLM-as-a-Judge
evidence.summary: Uses Krippendorff's alpha to measure both self-reliability and cross-judge agreement of LLM judges, exactly the metric and framing the proposal uses, applied generally rather than to scheming.

evidence.title: Constitutional Black-Box Monitoring for Scheming in LLM Agents
evidence.summary: Directly evaluates multiple judge models (GPT-5.1, Claude Sonnet 4.5, Gemini 2.5 Pro, Opus 4.5, Gemini 3 Pro) for scheming detection and reports cross-model variance (mean pAUROC variance < 0.02); covers judge-model sensitivity for scheming but measures detection accuracy vs ground truth, not inter-judge alpha on frozen transcripts or headline-rate swing across open judges.

evidence.title: Robustness of Model-Graded Evaluations and Automated Interpretability
evidence.summary: Studies how model-graded alignment/deception evaluations vary with grader model and inputs, establishing that evaluation outcomes are sensitive to judge choice in the alignment-eval setting.

evidence.title: Moral Mazes in the Era of LLMs
evidence.summary: Performs pairwise judge-agreement analysis holding the generator fixed and computes Krippendorff's alpha on PASS/FAIL labels across judge model pairs — the exact methodological template proposed, applied to a non-scheming task.

evidence.title: LLM-as-a-Judge sensitivity to evaluator model choice (Kinde / survey findings)
evidence.summary: Summarizes that evaluation results are highly sensitive to evaluator model choice with low inter-evaluator agreement and high variance, and that judges show systematic leniency offsets — the per-judge leniency phenomenon the proposal would measure.

evidence.title: Frontier Models are Capable of In-Context Scheming (Apollo Research)
evidence.summary: Apollo's scheming pipeline uses grader models to classify transcripts for covert action and reports grader accuracy checks against human labels; provides the transcript/grading substrate the proposal builds on but does not study inter-judge agreement across multiple open judges.
